points.label: Creation setting
points.left: The created world is presented as unfinished in experience even though Genesis describes creation as completed and very good.
points.right: The Bible’s closing vision uses creation language to describe a changed world and renewed divine-human dwelling.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: Creation personified · children of God · Futility → hoped-for freedom · Completed creation · groaning creation · Freedom from corruption
points.right: God dwells with people · New heaven · new earth · city · Former things pass → all things new · Death and pain absent · First creation · new creation

payload.posture: Both sources place present creation beside a future release from corruption, death, and pain.
payload.tension: Romans describes hope and groaning before release; Revelation announces a new heaven and earth after former things pass.
payload.title: Creation waits / all things made new
